title: Commit local records before rebuilding derived views
summary: Use transaction boundaries to distinguish durable source records from replaceable projections.
objectives: Verify rollback leaves no partial business record.
Separate a committed record from a derived graph view.

sources.title: SQLite transactions
sources.basis: BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK define the transaction boundary; error handling must decide when to roll back.

sections.title: A local transaction has one outcome
paragraphs: Write a synthetic record and its projection job in one transaction. A deliberate failure before commit must leave neither row present.
Commit success concerns local SQLite state. It does not establish that a graph projection, remote copy or backup completed.

sections.title: Derived views can be behind
paragraphs: A committed record may have a pending projection. Expose that state and rebuild from the canonical record instead of silently pretending both stores committed together.
Use an isolated temporary database for exercises. Product migrations, encrypted backup and power-loss recovery require their own acceptance.

exercise.instruction: Run the in-memory SQLite exercise. Force a transaction failure, then run a successful transaction.
exercise.expected: Rollback leaves zero records and zero jobs. Commit leaves one record and one pending job.

limitations: The test verifies SQLite transaction behavior in memory, not power-loss durability or an actual Graph adapter.
The pattern is educational; product schemas and authorization remain with their owners.
